stories.title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
stories.description: Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing1. Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses2. Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms3–5. However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics. A fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings the functionalities of fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification together in a single-step-grown platform is shown.

stories.title: A master gene for Drosophila male courtship prevents the behavior in females via a truncated protein
stories.description: Decades of studies have established that a terminal gene in the sex determination hierarchy, fruitless (fru), controls nearly all aspects of male courtship behaviors in Drosophila and many other insects. fru is transcribed in a sex-specific manner to produce male-specific Fru proteins (FruM) and was considered nonfunctional in females. In this study, we identify a female-specific truncated Fru protein (FruF) that is specifically expressed during the pupal stage and distributed in both cell bodies and neuronal projections, in contrast to FruM, which is expressed from larval to adult stages and localized to nuclei. We discover that FruF cooperates with another sex determination gene, doublesex (dsx), to prevent male-typical courtship in females. Knocking down fruF in dsx-expressing pC1 neurons induces courtship in females. These results reveal that the master gene for male courtship prevents this behavior in females via a truncated protein, thereby refining the canonical sex determination hierarchy that controls sexual development and behaviors. The fruitless gene has long been thought to function only in male flies to control male courtship. Peng et al. identify a transiently expressed, truncated Fruitless protein in females that suppresses male-typical courtship behaviour.

stories.title: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites
stories.description: Twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems. Although in-plane topological vortex nanostructures arising from twisting-induced lateral strain modulation have been linked to periodic moiré patterns in freestanding perovskite layers1–3 and 2D bilayers4, their coupling to the interfacial dislocation network in twisted layers remains unresolved. Here we demonstrate that twisted freestanding SrTiO3 (STO) layers undergo interfacial reconstruction into a network of screw dislocations, accompanied by the emergence of in-plane topological vortices. Unlike in previous reports, these vortices are associated with the dislocation network rather than with geometric moiré patterns. Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) reveals a beam deflection texture in registry with the interfacial dislocation network. A machine learning interatomic potential, trained on first-principles calculations, together with phase-field modelling, confirms that competing strains within the dislocation network stabilize polar vortex–antivortex pairs; first-principles calculations further reveal the emergence of an electronic superlattice with a well-defined periodicity. Our results establish twist-controlled dislocation networks as a new and versatile route to designing local polar and electronic structures in oxide materials. Experimental and theoretical investigation of twisted freestanding SrTiO3 layers using various analytic methods from 4DSTEM to DFT reveal a long-range ordered screw dislocation pattern as well as topological polar vortex arrays in the interface plane.

stories.title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
stories.description: van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1–4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7–12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures. An architecture comprising monolayer graphene doubly aligned to bulk and monolayer hBN on either side shows a gate-tunable global structural phase transition between two stacking configurations, accompanied by flat-band-induced integer doping.

stories.title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
stories.description: One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p-wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3). Achieving p-wave superconductivity4 and its magnetic analogue5—characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p-wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge6,7. Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p-wave magnets5,7–10, spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p-wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves Sy polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted Sy exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p-wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p-wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics10, topological matter7, superconductivity11 and beyond. A combination of symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations, neutron scattering and photoemission spectroscopy shows p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi.

stories.title: A novel SWO-optimized LBP-CNN-fuzzy approach for angiographic image enhancement and radiation dose reduction in cardiologists and patients
stories.description: Cardiac CT (CCT) is one of the most important and accurate tools in diagnosing coronary artery diseases and guiding cardiac surgeries. However, it is necessary to reduce the radiation dose to avoid damage caused by X-rays. The main problem in low-dose scans (LDCT) is the increase of quantum noise and the appearance of streak artifacts, which leads to a decrease in the quality of the images. In this research, improving the quality of angiographic images and reducing the radiation dose received by patients and cardiologists has been investigated using the LBP CNN FUZZY method optimized by the SWO spider bee optimization algorithm. In this new framework, a combination of fuzzy logic system, convolutional neural network (CNN) and local binary pattern (LBP) has been used to increase the contrast and improve the quality of the images. The first part of the framework consists of a parser network based on fuzzy logic and LBP, which decomposes the image into illumination and reflectance components. In the next step, the CNN-based adjustment network balances the exposure level by correcting the brightness component and reconstructs the colors with high fidelity. The meta-heuristic SWO algorithm guides the optimization steps of both parts and reduces noise and improves resolution in real time. The results of the experiments showed that the proposed method has a superior performance compared to the traditional methods, so that while obtaining better clarity and contrast in the images, the radiation dose received by the body was reduced by 72.15%. This approach can be effective in cardiac angiography to increase the quality of imaging and reduce the risk of radiation for patients and doctors.
